question.text: A plane electromagnetic wave with a frequency of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MHz</mi></math> travels in free space. At a particular point in space and time, the electric field is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The magnetic field at this point will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is,

solution.text: Recall the formula of the magnitude of the magnetic field in terms of the magnitude of the electric field, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>E</mi><mi>c</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>6</mn><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>, here <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>c</mi></math> is the speed of light in a vacuum.
